stem: A source of power $3.0\ \text{mW}$ operates for $4.0\ \text{ms}$; $50\%$ of its energy becomes $600\ \text{nm}$ light. How many photons are produced? Take $h=6.0\times10^{-34}\ \text{J s}$ and $c=3.0\times10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: Total energy = (3.0×10⁻³)(4.0×10⁻³) = 1.2×10⁻⁵ J; light energy = 6.0×10⁻⁶ J. Each photon has energy hc/λ = 3.0×10⁻¹⁹ J, giving 2.0×10¹³ photons.

working:
$E_{\text{light}}=0.50(3.0\times10^{-3})(4.0\times10^{-3})=6.0\times10^{-6}\ \text{J}$
$E_{\gamma}=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=\dfrac{(6.0\times10^{-34})(3.0\times10^8)}{600\times10^{-9}}=3.0\times10^{-19}\ \text{J}$
$N=\dfrac{E_{\text{light}}}{E_{\gamma}}=2.0\times10^{13}$

Independent check: Total energy = (3.0×10⁻³)(4.0×10⁻³) = 1.2×10⁻⁵ J; light energy = 6.0×10⁻⁶ J. Each photon has energy hc/λ = 3.0×10⁻¹⁹ J, giving 2.0×10¹³ photons.
solution:
The light energy is $E=0.50Pt=0.50(3.0\times10^{-3})(4.0\times10^{-3})=6.0\times10^{-6}\ \text{J}$.
Each photon has energy
$$E_\gamma=\frac{hc}{\lambda}=\frac{(6.0\times10^{-34})(3.0\times10^8)}{600\times10^{-9}}=3.0\times10^{-19}\ \text{J}.$$
Thus, $N=E/E_\gamma=2.0\times10^{13}$ photons.
